issues.title: Fixed-radius mesh convergence overclaim

failure_location.quote:
As $h_{\max}\to0$, $\overline{V}\to V$ and $\lambda_{k,h}^{R,\mathrm{P1}}\to\lambda_k^R$,
so the bounds converge to the true eigenvalues.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
As $h_{\max}\to0$, $\overline{V}\to V$ and $\lambda_{k,h}^{R,\mathrm{P1}}\to\lambda_k^R$,
so the bounds converge to the true eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that mesh refinement alone makes both finite-radius bounds converge exactly to the whole-space eigenvalue lambda_k. The old paper actually establishes that the upper endpoint converges to the finite-radius Dirichlet eigenvalue lambda_k^R; its lower endpoint likewise remains a finite-radius Neumann-based bound containing the fixed exterior correction in eq:bounds. The difference between lambda_k^R and lambda_k is separately identified as an R-dependent truncation error. Hence refinement removes discretization and coefficient-approximation errors but does not remove finite-R truncation or the old lower-bound correction.
issues.overall_effect: The rigorous enclosure in eq:bounds is not defeated, but its asymptotic interpretation is overstated: fixed-domain mesh refinement is presented as yielding exact whole-space eigenvalues even though finite-radius residuals remain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the convergence sentence with: “For fixed R, as h_max tends to zero, the upper endpoint tends to the finite-radius Dirichlet eigenvalue lambda_k^{R,Dir}, while the old lower endpoint tends to mu_k^{R,N}(V)(1-lambda_k^{R,Dir}/sigma(R)). Thus mesh refinement removes the discretization and coefficient-approximation errors, but finite-R truncation and the exterior correction remain; exact convergence to lambda_k requires R to tend to infinity as well.” No change to the rigorous enclosure itself is needed.
issues.why_classification: This is an invalid asymptotic inference, not a transcriptional error: Proposition prop:ub, equation eq:bounds, and Remark rem:agmon show that fixed-R limits retain both truncation and lower-bound correction terms. A short local qualification completely repairs the isolated prose claim without new proof architecture, but it necessarily withdraws the coherent substantive promise of exact convergence under mesh refinement alone. The surviving finite-radius or two-parameter convergence statement is recognizably comparable and the loss is limited, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

new_version_repair_locator.quote:
As $h_{\max}\to0$, $\overline{V}\to V$ and
$\lambda_{k,h}^{R,\mathrm{P1}}\to\lambda_k^{R,\mathrm{Dir}}$,
and both bounds converge to $\lambda_k$ (up to the exponentially
small Agmon truncation error discussed in
Remark~\ref{rem:agmon}).
